display.title: Episode 517: The Two Voices
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi teaches how to wash negel vasser with a story and song, a girl says the Shema in Studio 604, and Sarah learns there is no such thing as a small sin.
display.summary_long: Continuing the series on the Shulchan Aruch, Uncle Yossi reviews how to start the day: the first thought of Hashem, then Modeh Ani, then washing negel vasser, just as the Kohen washed before entering the Mishkan. A short story follows: little Zalman shows his mother the 'homework' he learned in class, pouring water three times on each hand and reciting the brachah, with a song to remember the mitzvah. With Purim getting closer, everyone joins the Hakochainik march. A student from a Brooklyn girls' school recites the Shema in Studio 604, and listeners put coins in the pushka. Story time, 'The Two Voices': on Shabbos afternoon Sarah finds a dime on the sidewalk and hears the yetzer hara urging her to pick it up and the yetzer tov warning her not to. Her father explains with a parable: a beggar cut a single rope in a rich man's attic and brought a magnificent chandelier crashing down. There is no such thing as a small sin. The show closes with an offer of a chart of the Twelve Pesukim, which the Rebbe asked every child to learn.
display.lesson: There is no such thing as a small sin: listen to the yetzer tov, not the yetzer hara, and do every mitzvah with joy.

date.note: Episode 518 is fixed to Tuesday 3 March 1992 by 'tomorrow night is Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni'; this is one week earlier, and 'getting closer to Purim' fits.
